scenes.title: Clinical human sleep EEG-fMRI suite: head coil closes and 20-second CSF waves surge during slow-wave sleep
scenes.era: 2019 Boston University Center for Biomedical Imaging nighttime EEG-fMRI laboratory

layout.description: Bright high-key clinical MRI scanner suite with a cylindrical white magnet bore, motorized cushioned scanner table, hinged white birdcage head coil over an unmarked EEG mesh cap, and an observation window looking onto a dual neuroimaging wave monitor.

positions.who: Sleeping volunteer (clothed matte-white porcelain figure with smooth featureless solid matte-white egg-shaped oval head in soft gray cotton scrubs and white mesh EEG cap)
positions.where: resting supine on the cushioned MRI scanner table inside the hinged white birdcage head coil

positions.who: Neuroimaging researcher (clothed matte-white porcelain figure with smooth featureless solid matte-white egg-shaped oval head in crisp white lab coat over navy sweater)
positions.where: standing beside the scanner table latching the birdcage head coil, then seated behind the observation glass watching coupled wave traces
positions.facing: facing the scanner table and observation console

props.name: cylindrical MRI scanner bore and hinged birdcage head coil
props.period_detail: smooth matte-white clinical magnet gantry with cushioned motorized table and open-lattice birdcage receiver coil
props.physical_behavior: hinged white head coil latches cleanly over the EEG cap before the motorized table glides smoothly into the illuminated bore

props.name: unmarked dual waveform display
props.period_detail: clean glass console displaying pure graphical blue CSF inflow waves locked to amber cortical slow waves with zero text
props.physical_behavior: as slow cortical waves dip, tall clear aqua fluid pulses rise rhythmically every twenty seconds

actions.verb_sequence: lowers the white birdcage head coil gently over the sleeper's EEG cap -> presses the unmarked table glide control so the cushioned bed slides smoothly into the bore

reactions.reaction: leans forward at the glass observation console as large rhythmic cerebrospinal fluid waves surge in lockstep with slow cortical waves

scenes.wardrobe: Volunteer in soft heather-gray cotton scrubs; researcher in crisp white lab coat over navy knit sweater and charcoal slacks.
scenes.lighting: Clean high-key clinical daylight balanced with soft warm tungsten rim light.
scenes.recognition_hook: Every twenty seconds during human deep sleep, cortical blood volume dips and a large wave of clear cerebrospinal fluid surges up into the brain.

key_visual.description: porcelain neuroimaging researcher lowers the white MRI birdcage head coil over a porcelain volunteer in a white EEG cap as the motorized scanner bed glides into the bright magnet bore

scenes.title: Conditioned bedroom hyperarousal vs 20-minute dim armchair stimulus-control reset
scenes.era: 1997-present everyday bedroom behavioral sleep experiment (Perlis & Bootzin model)

layout.description: Warm minimalist walnut bedroom with crisp oatmeal linen bedding on the left and a quiet corner reading armchair under a soft amber floor lamp on the right.

positions.who: Exhausted sleeper (clothed matte-white porcelain figure with smooth featureless solid matte-white egg-shaped oval head in slate-blue cotton pajamas)
positions.where: sitting bolt upright on rumpled linen sheets, then stepping calmly to the corner armchair with a plain paper book

props.name: walnut bed with crisp oatmeal linen sheets and dim amber floor lamp beside an upholstered armchair
props.period_detail: unmarked minimalist bedroom furniture with zero wall plaques or digital clocks
props.physical_behavior: sleeper folds back the linen duvet, steps out of bed to read a blank-paged hardcover under warm amber light until posture relaxes

actions.verb_sequence: grips the edge of the rumpled linen blanket in tense stillness -> rises calmly and settles into the dim amber-lit armchair holding an unmarked hardcover book

reactions.reaction: shoulders drop and head tilts gently forward as conditioned bedroom tension fades

scenes.wardrobe: Soft slate-blue cotton pajama shirt and trousers.
scenes.lighting: Soft architectural evening bedroom illumination with warm amber floor-lamp rim light.
scenes.recognition_hook: Staying awake frustrated in bed trains your cortex to treat the pillow like a threat alarm; stepping to a dim chair breaks the loop.

scenes.title: Natural 50-second norepinephrine vascular pump vs zolpidem sedative suppression
scenes.era: 2025 University of Copenhagen / Rochester vascular glymphatic imaging laboratory

layout.description: High-key modern neurobiology bench featuring a sculptural matte-white hinged vessel-sleeve teaching model alongside an unmarked amber pill blister tray left untouched.

positions.who: Lead investigator (clothed matte-white porcelain figure with smooth featureless solid matte-white egg-shaped oval head in white lab coat)
positions.where: demonstrating rhythmic vessel compression on the physical perivascular sleeve model

props.name: sculptural 3D perivascular vessel-sleeve model and unmarked amber blister pack
props.period_detail: matte-white articulated arterial sleeve model surrounded by star-shaped astrocytic endfeet
props.physical_behavior: gentle rhythmic compression of the inner vessel ring drives clear fluid pearls smoothly along the outer sleeve, while setting the sedative tray beside it holds the ring rigid

actions.verb_sequence: presses the articulated vessel ring in a slow rhythmic pulse -> slides the unmarked sedative blister tray aside on the oak bench

reactions.reaction: inclines head toward the model demonstrating that natural vascular pulsations, not chemical sedation, drive fluid flow

scenes.wardrobe: Crisp white laboratory coat over light chambray shirt.
scenes.recognition_hook: Sedative sleeping pills produce stillness while muting the slow norepinephrine blood-vessel pulses that pump rinse fluid through the brain.
